answer.headline: Covered months only: DFW leads West South Central airports on scheduled peak-hour intensity
answer.body:
A rank for the full requested calendar year cannot be established. The scheduled peak-hour metric comes from On-Time data, which does not cover January through August of that year. The ranking below uses the months of that year that are covered, September through December, and only airports in the West South Central census division that have this series.

From highest to lowest observed ninety-fifth percentile of scheduled peak hour (arrivals plus departures, reporting carriers, operated flights): DFW {F12}; IAH {F19}; AUS {F5}; DAL {F11}; HOU {F17}; MSY {F29}; SAT {F31}; OKC {F30}. ELP {F13} ties TUL {F36}. XNA {F40} ties LIT {F24}. Next is MAF {F26}. LBB {F21} ties SHV {F32}. Next is BTR {F8}. HRL {F18}, MFE {F27}, AMA {F4}, and CRP {F10} tie. Another tie covers LFT {F23}, AEX {F3}, LRD {F25}, BRO {F7}, GRK {F16}, ABI {F1}, LCH {F22}, CLL {F9}, ACT {F2}, TYR {F38}, SJT {F33}, LAW {F20}, TXK {F37}, GGG {F15}, SWO {F35}, and BPT {F6}. The lowest tied group is MLU {F28}, FSM {F14}, SPS {F34}, and VCT {F39}.

These figures are observed. They are not a forecast, an annualized full-year statistic, or an investment score. Equal values are ties; consecutive positions the rank tool assigned inside a tie are not a further ordering.

claims.text: For September through December of the requested year, West South Central airports with an observed scheduled peak-hour series rank as follows, highest to lowest: DFW {F12}, IAH {F19}, AUS {F5}, DAL {F11}, HOU {F17}, MSY {F29}, SAT {F31}, OKC {F30}, then ELP {F13} tied with TUL {F36}, then XNA {F40} tied with LIT {F24}, then MAF {F26}, then LBB {F21} tied with SHV {F32}, then BTR {F8}, then HRL {F18} tied with MFE {F27}, AMA {F4}, and CRP {F10}, then LFT {F23} tied with AEX {F3}, LRD {F25}, BRO {F7}, GRK {F16}, ABI {F1}, LCH {F22}, CLL {F9}, ACT {F2}, TYR {F38}, SJT {F33}, LAW {F20}, TXK {F37}, GGG {F15}, SWO {F35}, and BPT {F6}, then MLU {F28} tied with FSM {F14}, SPS {F34}, and VCT {F39}.

The metric is the ninety-fifth percentile over date and local hour of scheduled arrivals plus departures for operated flights. On the DFW finding it is observed, and it is a lower bound on total scheduled operations because On-Time includes domestic flights of reporting carriers only.

The same metric definition was applied to every airport in this rank, so the order compares that lower-bound scheduled peak, not total airport operations. It does not establish which airport has more unmet demand, tighter terminal capacity, or a stronger modernization case.

assumptions: West South Central is the Census division of that name. Entity resolution matched that division exactly.
The full requested calendar year is outside On-Time coverage, so the rank uses September through December of that year, the covered slice, with no annualization.
Airports are ordered by the observed peak-hour metric. Relative points produced by the rank tool are a calculated rescaling within the set and are not treated as the result.
limitations: January through August of the requested year are missing from On-Time coverage, so a full-year ninety-fifth percentile cannot be computed. The full-year order is unknown.
The series excludes international flights and small carriers, and it is not a tower-operation count.
On-Time coverage inside the window is incomplete on the DFW finding. Coverage ratios for the other airports were not separately retrieved, so sparse reporting could affect some percentiles.
Division airports with no series for this metric, including AFW, FTW, HRO, and HOT, plus many smaller airports, are omitted. Omission means missing data, not a measured peak of zero.
Terminal capacity, unmet demand, fares, and profitability are not measured. This is a metric rank, not a screening valuation.
